questions.answer: Protons with positive charge and neutrons with no net charge are in the nucleus. Negatively charged electrons orbit outside the nucleus.
accepted_alternatives: The nucleus contains positive protons and uncharged neutrons, with negative electrons outside it.
questions.tolerance: Equivalent particle locations and charges accepted.

marking_points.text: States that protons are positively charged and are in the nucleus
States that neutrons have no net charge and are in the nucleus
States that negatively charged electrons orbit outside the nucleus

option_feedback.A: Correct: frequent transmission shows that most atomic volume contains no concentrated matter.
option_feedback.B: The rare repulsion of positive alpha particles supports a positive nucleus, not a negative one.
option_feedback.C: Nearly all atomic mass is concentrated in the nucleus, not in electrons.
option_feedback.D: A nucleus occupying most of the volume would cause many more deflections.

marking_points.text: Selects A, inferring that most of the atom is empty space

option_feedback.A: Opposite charges attract, so spread-out negative charge would not cause the observed strong repulsion.
option_feedback.B: Correct: close approach to concentrated positive charge produces strong repulsion.
option_feedback.C: Neutrons are in the nucleus and have no net charge.
option_feedback.D: An empty region cannot exert the strong force needed for a large deflection.

marking_points.text: Selects B, identifying a small region of concentrated positive charge

option_feedback.A: Electrons orbit outside the nucleus rather than being in it.
option_feedback.B: Protons are also in the nucleus.
option_feedback.C: Correct: protons and neutrons form the nucleus and electrons orbit outside.
option_feedback.D: Electrons are outside while protons and neutrons are inside the nucleus.

marking_points.text: Selects C, placing protons and neutrons in the nucleus and electrons outside

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Most of the atom is empty space, or the nucleus occupies a very small fraction of atomic volume.
accepted_alternatives: Most atomic volume contains no concentrated matter.

marking_points.text: Infers from the many straight paths that most of the atom is empty space

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: The alpha particle is positive and is strongly repelled, so the nucleus is positively charged. Because such paths are rare, the nucleus is very small. The large deflection shows that nearly all atomic mass is concentrated in the nucleus.

marking_points.text: Infers that the nucleus is positively charged from strong repulsion of a positive alpha particle
Infers from the rarity of the large deflection that the nucleus is very small
Infers from the large deflection that nearly all atomic mass is concentrated in the nucleus

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons, and electrons are outside the nucleus.
parts.tolerance: One mark for each stated correct feature.

marking_points.text: Identifies that protons and neutrons are in the nucleus
Identifies that electrons are outside the nucleus

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: Most alpha particles pass through with little or no deflection, showing that most atomic volume is empty. If the nucleus filled half the atom, many particles would meet concentrated matter and be strongly deflected, so the nucleus must be much smaller.
parts.tolerance: Equivalent contradiction using scattering evidence accepted.

marking_points.text: Uses the observation that most alpha particles pass through with little or no deflection
Explains that the observation requires the nucleus to occupy a very small fraction of atomic volume

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: X has little or no deflection. Y has a moderate deflection. Z has the largest deflection and may turn back because it approaches closest to the nucleus.

marking_points.text: Predicts little or no deflection for X and a greater deflection for Y
Predicts the largest deflection for Z because it approaches closest to the nucleus

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: The alpha particle has positive charge and the nucleus has positive charge. Like charges repel, so the alpha particle is repelled as it approaches the nucleus.
parts.tolerance: Both charge identification and repulsion required.

marking_points.text: States that both the alpha particle and the nucleus are positively charged
Explains that like charges repel, causing Z to deflect away from the nucleus

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: Protons and neutrons are in the tiny central nucleus. Electrons orbit outside the nucleus in the much larger surrounding atomic region.

marking_points.text: Places protons and neutrons in the central nucleus
Places electrons orbiting outside the nucleus
